subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron and heartbeat authority be implemented as narrow per-job/heartbeat metadata, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The choice changes host-exec trust boundaries, cron storage/protocol shape, heartbeat semantics, audit expectations, and compatibility for users currently relying on wildcard cron-event or heartbeat elevation.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Use one authority model across cron APIs, execution receipts, heartbeat state, audit, and migration so scheduled agent actions have non-forgeable provenance.

options.title: Add Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat elevated markers now, accepting the risk of a separate authority model from the broader scheduling provenance RFC.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove broad internal-source elevation and require explicit operator reconfiguration, accepting upgrade friction for existing unattended workflows.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Use one authority model across cron APIs, execution receipts, heartbeat state, audit, and migration so scheduled agent actions have non-forgeable provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Closest recent owner of the cron/Gateway caller-scope security boundary that overlaps this decision.
